content:
maya: Heads-up — noticed large queue growth on us-west1 around 18:05 UTC, correlates with 3 preemptible GPU evictions. TPM dropped but incoming request rate stayed high. :rotating_light:
ops-bot: autoscaler: evicted 3 preemptible nodes in cluster-west-1 (reason: preemptible-reclaim)
dmitri: Can you paste the numbers? GPUs before/after and the observed TPM/RPM?
maya: Before: 120 GPUs, after: 117. Using our per-GPU baseline we expect ~100 TPM per GPU for the medium model -> theoretical capacity 12k TPM -> now ~11.7k TPM. But our token-accounting showed allowed TPS didn't change for ~3m so queueed tasks spiked.
jules: That mismatch is the crux — admission control used a stale snapshot of capacity and we don't atomically reduce the token bucket on node eviction.
kevin: Agreed. We're currently doing a periodic capacity poll every 60s, and then scaling token refill accordingly. With evictions the polling granularity is too coarse.
maya: Right. Impact: backlog grew to ~2.4k requests (p99 latency > 12s), a few timeouts from customer-facing routes. Alert: fleet.backpressure.high_queue fired.
sre-oncall: I temporarily set the route limiter to 0.9 of reported capacity to be conservative. That calmed the queue but customer throughput dropped. :thumbsup:
dmitri: Long-term fix ideas: 1) move to event-driven capacity updates on node lifecycle (kube events). 2) fast-path token drain when available_gpus decreases. 3) add EWMA smoothing to avoid oscillation.
tara: For 2) we should compute an "effective_tpm" that floors to integer GPUs: effective_tpm = available_gpus * per_gpu_tpm. When available_gpus drops, we immediately scale refill_rate = effective_tpm / 60 (tokens/sec), clamp to max 0.95 * effective_tpm to leave headroom.
jules: Also need to account for model mix — not every request is medium model. We weight by recent request distribution. New formula: effective_tpm = sum_over_models(available_gpus * per_gpu_tpm_for_model * model_share). That prevents overcommit when many heavy model requests appear.
kevin: Implementation note: per_gpu_tpm_for_model is dynamic based on batch size and quantization profile. Use the compiled kernel profile to get a conservative estimate.
dmitri: Suggested rollout: patch admission controller to subscribe to node events, update capacity snapshot immediately on eviction, and apply smoothing window of 30s with alpha=0.2 for increase but immediate drop for decreases (fast-fail). That prevents slow ramp-ups but reacts fast to capacity loss.
maya: Here's an emergency policy snippet I tested locally — it prevents the token bucket from granting more than capacity during sudden drops:```yaml
admission_control:
  refill_window_secs: 60
  per_gpu_tpm: 100
  safety_factor: 0.95
  smoothing:
    increase_alpha: 0.2
    decrease_immediate: true
```
dmitri: Love it. Also add a policy to fallback to a cheaper model variant when queue depth > 80% of buffer and capacity < threshold. Example: if queue_ratio > 0.8 AND available_gpus < 0.8*baseline -> route to quantized variant.
tara: We should publish the exact math to docs for SREs: show how we compute token refill from GPU counts and model mix, and how to tune safety_factor.
kevin: One more gotcha — preemptible node evictions can be batched by the cloud for a single AZ, which reduces not just count but regional network egress capacity. Admission control must consider per-AZ capacity too, not only total GPUs (we had a tiny spike in cross-AZ retries).
jules: Good call. Add az-aware tokens: tokens_az = available_gpus_az * per_gpu_tpm and then admission controller enforces both global and az-local caps.
sre-oncall: I've opened an incident doc and linked dashboard panels: fleet > capacity > per-az GPUs and token refill. Also created ticket INFRA-412 to implement node-event-driven updates and the EWMA policy.
maya: Postmortem plan: short-term (hotfix) = conservative safety_factor and immediate node-event hook; mid-term = model-mix weighting + az-aware caps + fallback to quantized.
dmitri: For the token-accounting code: avoid races by performing a CAS update on the capacity token bucket. Pseudocode:```go
old := atomic.LoadUint64(&capacity)
new := computeFromNodes()
if new < old { atomic.StoreUint64(&capacity, new) } else { // smooth increase
  atomic.StoreUint64(&capacity, old + uint64(alpha*(float64(new-old))))
}
```
kevin: Also add an alert that watches for tokens_granted > capacity_snapshot for > 10s — that's a symptom of race.
tara: I'll update runbook with these mitigation steps and include the YAML snippet and the CAS pseudocode.
maya: Thanks team — we'll schedule the patch for tomorrow's infra release and spin a canary in us-west1 first. I'll keep the channel updated. :rocket:
